newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sumitomo Trust says overseas operations in black.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo Trust says overseas operations in black.

text.p: Sumitomo Trust & Banking Co Ltd's overseas business was roughly in the black in the fiscal year that ended on March 31 and the bank will continue to strengthen and expand its overseas operations, Sumitomo Trust managing director Takenori Osakabe told reporters on Wednesday.
"Overseas operations are a pillar of the bank and we'll strengthen and expand them," Osakabe said.
He strongly denied various market rumours on Wednesday that the company had incurred large foreign exchange losses and that it was withdrawing from overseas operations.
"We want market participants to make proper judgements (about the bank)," he said.
The bank will continue to consider fund-raising while watching market conditions, although any details remain undecided, he said.
Asked if Sumitomo Trust is planning to issue preferred stock, Osakabe said the bank will consider every possible scheme for its fund raising, but nothing has been decided yet.
Trade in Sumitomo Trust's shares was suspended on the Tokyo Stock Exchange this morning amid rumours that it was considering equity financing worth some 100 billion yen.
On Monday, underwriting sources told Reuters the trust bank was considering issuing euroyen convertible bonds worth some 100 billion yen in an attempt to strengthen its asset base.
But some underwriting sources said at that time that a lack of clear direction in the stock market could make the timing of the issue uncertain.
